thread:
Jake: Heads-up — planned rollout tonight 02:00 UTC: API v2.3 + runtime kernel update. Need console + router pin walk before canary. DeployBot will start canary at 02:10.
Anya: Copy. I'll pin console to 2.3-rc and check dashboard prefetch behavior.
Maria: Router needs header-split change for the new API header. Also prefetched KV keys might be invalidated on deploy — can we add a prewarm step?
Sam: Runtime change is the kernel batch switch + KV eviction tweak. Behavior change expected only during warmup, not correctness.
DeployBot: Scheduled wave: canary=5% (02:10-02:20), rollout to 25% at 02:30 unless canary health crosses thresholds. Health checks: 5xx < 0.5%, p95 < 500ms.
Jake: Proposed prefetch step after canary warmup: run prefetch job against canary subset. Command for ops: ```POST /internal/prefetch?scope=canary -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP'``` run as one-off.
Anya: Console will run the prefetch job, but we need router to accept the probing path (internal-prefetch). Router owners, can you add a routing rule that pins that path to the canary group?
Nina: Router: can add temporary route /internal-prefetch -> canary. Queuing change now, ETA ~8m. Will also add a short TTL to avoid long-lived pinning.
Maria: I'll add a fallback flag in console so if prefetch misses it uses cached results; that avoids user-visible regressions. Will also add a short note in release notes.
Sam: We'll emit X-KV-Fallback: true on fallback to help console detect misses. Also adding a metric kv.prefetch.miss to track.
DeployBot: Canary started. Initial health: 0/50 failures. Monitoring p50/p95.
DeployBot: Canary update: 1/50 checks failing — p50 spike to 650ms, p95 710ms. Not 5xx. Marking canary as HOLD.
Jake: Pausing rollout. Is this kernel warmup noise or something else? Thoughts?
Nina: Router logs show no surge in 5xx, just latency on /generate endpoints. Likely kernel/jit warmup. Could be batching thresholds mis-tuned for small seq lengths.
Maria: Console prefetch job shows ~10% misses during canary warmup window but no 5xx. I can flip fallback on immediately to suppress surface-level impact.
Sam: Plan: if p95 > 600ms after 10m, we'll roll back the kernel flag. Otherwise, let it stabilize and re-run prefetch. I'm also toggling a slower batch ramp to smooth warmup.
Jake: Decision: hold, enable console fallback, re-evaluate in 10m. No immediate rollback. Update release notes with note: "Known warmup latency for kernel change; console prefetch fallback enabled as mitigation."
Anya: Updated console pin + prefetch job run queued. I'll ping when results are stable.
Maria: I turned on fallback flag; prefetch miss rate dropped from 10% -> 2% on canary. Users should be unaffected.
Sam: After batch ramp tweak p95 down to 480ms on canary. DeployBot: canary health good, recommending resume to 25% at 02:30.
DeployBot: Resuming rollout. Track kv.prefetch.miss and X-KV-Fallback headers for next 3 hours.
Jake: Thanks all. I'll add a post-release note in the changelog about the kernel warmup and the mitigation steps (prefetch + fallback + batch-ramp). If any unexpected 5xx crop up, open an incident in #incidents and tag eng-sre.
Anya: Will follow up with a short how-to for customers who run private infra (prefetch endpoint + fallback header).
Nina: Router rule cleaned up after canary; temporary route removed.
DeployBot: Rollout to 25% complete, scheduled full rollout at 03:00 if no regressions.
